narrationScript: Welcome to Chapter 2.3: File I/O and Command-Line Arguments. In this vital chapter, we'll dive into how C programs can interact with the outside world beyond just temporary memory. Our goals are clear: First, you'll understand why file input/output is essential for data persistence, allowing your programs to save and retrieve information. Second, you'll learn the core C library functions to open, read from, write to, and close files safely. Third, we'll cover how to handle common file I/O errors and detect the end of a file. Finally, we'll explore command-line arguments, mastering how to parse user input directly from the terminal using `argc` and `argv` to make your programs more flexible and powerful.
